subject.title: [Bug]: Isolated cron agentTurn fails with 'setup timed out before runner start' — all fallback models exhausted on 2026.5.12

question: Should OpenClaw accept a bounded longer default setup watchdog for isolated cron agent turns, or require a different product shape such as a lower cap or operator-tunable config?
rationale: The code fix is focused, but it intentionally changes how long a stuck isolated setup may hold cron capacity before recovery; that default availability tradeoff needs maintainer intent.

options.title: Land the bounded watchdog fix
options.body: Accept the 60s floor, half-job-timeout budget, and 10m cap from the open PR as the default fix for busy-host false setup timeouts.

options.title: Require a tighter bound
options.body: Ask the PR to use a lower cap or stronger setup-progress proof before changing the default timeout window.

options.title: Defer to explicit configurability
options.body: Keep the 60s default for now and require a separate product-approved config knob for operators who need longer setup windows.

recommendation.title: Land the bounded watchdog fix
recommendation.body: Accept the 60s floor, half-job-timeout budget, and 10m cap from the open PR as the default fix for busy-host false setup timeouts.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merged cron watchdog work and broader isolated-runtime maintenance make this the strongest available routing signal for the product/default tradeoff.
